text:
alex: Quick summary from today's offline replays — ran the preemptive-queue + token-budget target changes against 3 week trace sample (prod-synth-2026-02). Wanted to drop notes and get eyes on a weird 95p regression.

maria: awesome, drop the numbers plz. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: TL;DR: mean throughput up ~6% on bursty chat traces, overall cost per token down ~3%, but observed 95p latency +8% after we switched kernel-affinity selection in the runtime shim. CPU/GPU scheduling looks correlated.

shivani: hmm that smells like kernel scheduling interacting with continuous batching. Did you preserve queue priors?

alex: yes, queue priors identical. The change was: earlier kernel selector used round-robin fallback which favored smaller batches on some GPUs; new selector biases affinity to the last used kernel to improve KV cache locality.

maria: can you paste the exact replayer command and config used?

alex: sure:
```
./replayer --trace prod-synth-2026-02 --duration 72h --mode offline --policy preemptive-queue --token-budget 12 --kernel-selector affinity
```
and the important snippet from the policy file:
```yaml
queue_policy: preemptive
token_budget_target: 12  # tokens per request bucket
kernel_selector: affinity   # affinity preserves last kernel to try to keep KV warm
max_batch_wait_ms: 8
```

perf-bot: [run 2018456789] replay finished: 72h simulated, 1.2M requests, 8.3% increase in 95p latency vs baseline, 6.1% throughput gain, 3.2% cost/unit reduction. (see /perf/results/2018456789)

shivani: logs? gpu kv hit rate?

alex: kv hit rate went up ~4% in affinity runs, but we observed more batch size variance — lots of small batches hitting late due to preemptive dispatch when token budgets were exhausted. That combination seems to push a subset of requests into higher tail.

dan: do you have a breakdown by route/model? Could be one model with long ctxs causing token budget starvation across queue slices.

alex: yep. Breakdown: chat-short (60% traffic) latency stable; chat-long (18%) 95p +22%; embeders (22%) slight improvement. So skewed tail on long requests.

maria: sounds like token-budget target might be too aggressive for long requests. If preemptive-queue drains slices early, long ctx requests get starved and end up in tiny batches that hit expensive kernels.

shivani: proposal: two arms in A/B harness — keep affinity + higher token_budget_target for long-ctx cohort (e.g., 20) vs affinity+12 baseline. Also add a micro-delay (2-3ms) cap for preemptive dispatch for long-ctx queue to let batches form.

alex: I ran a quick replay variant with token_budget=20 just for chat-long cohort. Results: 95p for chat-long dropped from +22% to +3% vs baseline, throughput change negligible, cost +0.8% on that cohort.

perf-bot: [run 2018456890] sub-run: token_budget=20 for chat-long -> 95p delta +3.1%, kv_hit +5.2%, cost +0.8% on cohort (global cost delta +0.2%).

dan: nice. We should also instrument kernel latency distribution per batch-size. Affinity might be causing some kernels to be picked that have worse small-batch perf for long-ctx requests.

alex: good call. I pulled kernel latencies: small-batch (<8 tokens) latency for kernel X (affinity preferred) is ~1.6x of kernel Y which RR sometimes picked. For big batches kernel X is better. So tradeoff exists.

maria: can we make kernel_selector aware of batch-size heuristics? e.g., affinity but fall back to kernel that optimized for small batch if batch_size < threshold. That should preserve kv locality for big batches and avoid small-batch tail.

shivani: and add a coldness metric for KV cache per kernel. If kv_coldness > 0.25 then prefer kernel Y. We can compute kv_coldness in runtime periodically.

alex: agreed. I can push two changes for the next replay: (1) kernel_selector: affinity-with-batch-threshold, threshold=8, (2) token_budget_target: cohort-aware (12/20) plus preemptive-delay-ms: 3 for long.

maria: also add these to A/B harness config. Target sample size for the A/B should be 100k requests per arm for stable 95p estimate.

dan: will add dashboard panels: per-model 95p, kv_hit, batch_size_dist, kernel_choice_frac.

alex: action items:
- alex: implement affinity-with-batch-threshold in runtime shim and wire a flag (ETA: tomorrow afternoon)
- alex: run full 72h replay with cohort token_budget 12/20 + preemptive-delay 3ms (ETA: Friday morning)
- dan: add dashboard panels and hook A/B harness to split traces (ETA: EOD today)
- shivani: propose kv_coldness metric + threshold (ETA: EOD)

maria: thanks. If the Friday replay looks like the quick run, we can roll a limited canary to dedicated and monitor real 95p. :fast_forward:

alex: cool — I'll post the full replay artifacts and a short runbook in this thread when ready.

perf-bot: note: tagging the perf-alert channel for follow-up: @perf-alert :bell:

maria: :thumbsup:
